intent: The freeform text answer of a QuestionnaireItem, rendered as the kit Input.
typical_uses: The only answer of an item with no choices
A freeform "other" answer after an item's fixed choices

dont_use_when.situation: A text field in an ordinary form outside a questionnaire

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

The field counts as the item's answer once its text is non-blank after trimming, and is stamped `data-filled` or `data-empty`; it submits under the item's name only while it is the item's answer, so blank text, a skipped item or a choice checked after it in a single-answer item submit nothing from it.
Without `render` it renders the kit Input; `render` replaces that element entirely.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave both to the questionnaire; the field submits under its item's `name`, and its props omit both

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the field's own state (`QuestionnaireInputState`: disabled, filled, invalid), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted. The kit defaults it to its own Input.

good.title: A freeform "other" answer after fixed choices
good.code:
<QuestionnaireChoices>
  <QuestionnaireChoice value="approvals">Approval checkpoints</QuestionnaireChoice>
  <QuestionnaireInput aria-label="Another feature" placeholder="Describe another feature" />
</QuestionnaireChoices>

bad.title: The kit Input in place of QuestionnaireInput
bad.why: A plain Input is not registered with the item, so typing never marks the item answered and Next keeps failing its validation.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireInputState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the field's own state (`QuestionnaireInputState`: disabled, filled, invalid), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted. The kit defaults it to its own Input.
